nodes.title: Map boards (main's decision, option b): places pinned at their TRUE latitude/longitude on a labelled 5° degree grid with a compass, and NO outline of any kind: no country, state, coastline or region shape, from memory or from data, because an Indian product must show India's official boundaries and none is sourced yet. places@1 draws only a frame, edge ticks, small crosses where grid lines meet, degree labels, a compass, the Tropic of Cancer / 82.5°E meridian when the kit names them, and pins with names. Every pin comes from data/geo/india-places.json (61 places; cities from Natural Earth 1:10m populated places, public domain; heritage sites, Kanyakumari and Darjeeling from Wikidata P625, CC0; each row names its source record; built by scripts/build-india-places.mjs). Option (a), an official outline, waits on the owner (on main's decision list).
nodes.reversal: an owner-approved, provenance-recorded Survey of India outline is committed

nodes.title: places@1 (C1 item 5, India map places): places.js picks a science/SST/EVS kit naming ≥ 3 gazetteer places (never a maths word problem), up to 6 in the kit's order and words ('Bombay' stays Bombay). Frame = the places' extent padded 2.5°, snapped to 5°, one scale both ways, widened ≤ 10° toward the board's room. Names are laid out before anything is drawn: beside the pin, else 30/52 units out on a leader that crosses nothing; a grid cross a name needs the room of is left out; a place whose name fits nowhere is left off (her line is written only from what is drawn); a named line whose name fits nowhere is left off. Gate change: W4 treats ≥ 3 evenly spaced degree labels of one direction ('15°N', '20°N', '25°N', each the whole text) as an AXIS, like a number line's ticks; a lone or uneven degree is still checked. Explain ladder: after label@1, before the library. Recordings docs/design/round7/studio/map-*.

nodes.method: placesCall over every class 1-9 science/SST/EVS kit; expand + retime to an 8 s line naming the drawn places + gateWhiteboard with the kit; the template explainerFor returns; code only, no model calls
nodes.title: 33 kits name ≥ 3 places; 33/33 boards pass every W gate; places@1 is the board drawn in 29 (the rest keep an earlier rung, e.g. a timeline). 138 of the 147 named places are pinned; the 9 left off are near neighbours (Delhi/Jaipur/Panipat/Shimla, Ajanta/Ellora, Patna/Pataliputra) or a long name at the frame's edge (Thiruvananthapuram). The Tropic / 82.5°E lines are drawn in every kit that names them.

tests/p4-content-unit 'board sync: the line plan wins inside the deadline' (App: failed under single-process npm test load, 28/28 alone): the speculative-board half asserted syncMs < 900; now it asserts ORDER (the spec board answered before the 2 s line plan landed). 8 parallel copies: 8/8 pass.

md.decisions:
## dc-r7-maps-no-outline: maps show places on a degree grid, no outline (2026-11-04)

Map boards pin places at their true latitude and longitude on a labelled grid with a compass. They draw no outline of India, its states or its coast, because an official, sourced boundary is required and none has been provided yet. Reversal: an owner-approved, provenance-recorded Survey of India outline is committed.

## dc-r7-board-places-template: the places board (2026-11-04)

When a geography, history or EVS lesson names three or more places, the board shows them on that grid, in the lesson's own words, with the Tropic of Cancer or the 82.5°E meridian when the lesson mentions them.
md.measurements:
## ms-r7-board-places-reach (2026-11-04, n = 33 kits)

33 lessons name three or more places; all 33 boards pass the board gates and 29 now show the map. 138 of 147 named places are pinned; the rest sit too close to a neighbour to label.
